Subject: Egress stalls post cutover - intermittent connectivity to S3

Hi Priya,

We completed the private deployment cutover in us-west-2 last night and are seeing intermittent egress stalls from a subset of our app hosts to S3. Symptoms: sudden burst of TCP timeouts for 10-30s, then flows recover; traceroutes from host show next-hop reachable but packets are dropped intermittently. We captured one pcap (attached) and a brief arp dump from the CPE.

This started ~01:30 UTC and has been recurring across two app instances. Can the Redwood team take a look? We suspect something in SNAT path or ARP aging interplay with our CPE.

Subject: Re: Egress stalls post cutover - intermittent connectivity to S3

Quick analysis after ingesting the pcap and the CPE arp dump. Observations: 1) Repeated ARP requests for the same Redwood egress gateway IP with no ARP reply for ~12-18s in several windows. 2) During those windows we see TCP SYN retransmits from app host, while traces inside our fabric show the packet reached the GW but egress translation state (SNAT map) was missing and then re-created (seen in redwood-snat-state.log). 3) The pattern aligns with CPE doing aggressive ARP cache pruning (short timeout) combined with transient SNAT mappings expiring under low-traffic tails. When ARP is missing the CPE re-ARP which temporarily drops established flows until mapping is re-provisioned.

Hypothesis: ARP timeout on the CPE is shorter than our expected keepalive/refresh for ephemeral SNAT entries. When the CPE ages out the MAC for the gateway the forwarded packet gets lost until ARP completes and SNAT mapping is rehydrated.

Recommended immediate actions (can be applied without infra-wide maintenance):
- Increase ARP cache timeout on CPE to >= 60s (current shows ~20s). See cpe-arp-cache.txt snapshot for current values.
- For Redwood egress: extend ephemeral SNAT TTL from 30s -> 120s for this customer route (we can do per-tenant override).
- Add a light ARP keepalive from a control probe on app hosts (small UDP ping every 20s) while we monitor.

I attached the SNAT state extract (redwood-snat-state.log) and a one-line playbook diff that implements the per-tenant SNAT TTL increase. If the above changes stop the events we can schedule a more conservative permanent change and update the runbook.

Attachments: redwood-snat-state.log, runbook-playbook-diff.txt

-Karthik
